messages.subject: Anyone installed Stan or RStan on Columbia Cluster?
parts:
Hi all,

Does any of you successfully install Stan or Rstan on the Hotfoot High Performance Computing (HPC) Cluster? I tried to install Stan from the command line and install Rstan inside R on the cluster, but neither works out. Are there any requirements that I ignore?

Thanks!
Yajuan

> make: *** [bin/stan/command/stanc.o] Error 1

This is presumably just what it says it is -- that g++
ran out of memory. Do you know how much memory there
is on each node of the cluster? Stan/RStan needs quite
a lot of memory to compile (as much as 3GB, I think).

It might take less memory if you can build it with -O2 or -O1
optimization (but then it'll be slower to run). You might
also try squeezing it in using the clang++ compiler.

- Bob

This is the same out-of-memory error from g++ as
compiling Stan directly. But it's after libstan.a
gets built. At this point, you can definitely use
optimization level 0 to build bin/stanc.

You could also talk to somebody who knows how to configure the
cluster to see if you can get more memory.

Or it might be possible to compile a binary
somewhere else that you can use on the cluster -- Ben or someone
involved in the cluster might know how to do that or if it'd
even be feasible.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Anyone installed Stan or RStan on Columbia Cluster?
parts:
Jon had installed rstan on the hotfoot before. I guess the version of gcc is still less than 4.2.1.  You can see the version of gcc by executing 'gcc -v', which might be helpful to identify the problem. 

But there is a gcc44 installed on hotfoot, which is not the default one.  So in Stan, you need to add "CC=g++44" after "make bin/stanc". 

For R, you need to create, in your home directory, a new directory (unless it already exists):

mkdir .R

and then within this new directory, with your favorite editor, create a file named "Makevars", containing the following two lines.

CXX = g++44
SHLIB_CXXLD = g++44

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Anyone installed Stan or RStan on Columbia Cluster?
parts:
On Sunday, April 21, 2013 10:07:39 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Or it might be possible to compile a binary
somewhere else that you can use on the cluster -- Ben or someone
involved in the cluster might know how to do that or if it'd
even be feasible.

The default g++ on Hotfoot is 4.1.2 which is not known to have ever worked (in addition to the possible memory problems). So, you need to explicitly specify g++4.4 on the command line to have a fighting chance. Or if trying to install RStan, you need a file in $HOME/.R/Makevars that contains at least these lines

CC=gcc44
CXX=g++44

I doubt the cluster is binary compatible with anything I have, but dropping a binary in might be possible in principle.

Ben
